venue.name: Pacific Rim National Park Reserve
venue.description: Pacific Rim National Park Reserve sits on the rugged west coast of Vancouver Island and is made up of three units: the Long Beach Unit, the Broken Group Islands Unit and the West Coast Trail Unit. The park's own activities page lists hiking, beaches, bird watching, cycling, surfing, storm watching, interpretive programs and school programs among the things to do. The ʔapsčiik t̓ašii multi-use pathway extends 25 km from the southern to the northern boundary of the Long Beach Unit and is used on foot, by stroller, by wheelchair and by bicycle. Guided activities and tours in all units of the park are available from licensed commercial operators rather than from the park itself.

facility_notes.stroller_accessible: Explore the ʔapsčiik t̓ašii on foot, stroller, wheelchair, or bicycle. The multi-use pathway extends 25 km from the southern to the northern boundary of the Long Beach Unit.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: Explore the ʔapsčiik t̓ašii on foot, stroller, wheelchair, or bicycle.

restrictions: Interim restrictions have been implemented for custodial groups kayaking or canoeing in Pacific Rim's marine waters. Please contact the park prior to arrival for information and appropriate permits.
A custodial group means a group affiliated with an institution, where at least one person is below the age of majority and a minor is unaccompanied by his/her parent or guardian.
Collecting natural (e.g., wildflowers, rocks, mushrooms, berries) or cultural objects (e,g., First Nation or early settlers artifacts)
Kite flying in the Long Beach North and Incinerator beaches (along the airport approach way)
Activities involving aircraft, including Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs, or drones) except with a Restricted Activity Permit
venue.seasonal_notes: The Kʷisitis area at the south end of Wickaninnish Beach will be closed to the public from Wednesday, September 16 to Friday, September 25, 2026, inclusive, in recognition of Yuułuʔiłʔatḥ’s historical and modern connection to their ḥaw̓iiḥ ḥaḥuułi (hereditary chiefs’ territory). This closure includes the Kʷisitis Visitor Centre, the Kʷisitis Visitor Centre parking lot, the South Beach trail, the Nuu-chah-nulth trail, and the southern end of Wickaninnish Beach (including Lismer Beach and South Beach).

programs.name: School programs
programs.description: Pacific Rim National Park Reserve lists school programs among the things to do in the park. The park's own school programs page could not be reached, so what the programs cover, which ages or grades they are for, how long they run, what they cost and how to book them are all unknown here.
programs.our_note: Treat this one as a phone call rather than a booking page. Ask what ages it suits, whether a preschool group fits, and what it costs on top of getting into the park.
programs.practical_summary: None of the practical detail for this program is available. Ages, cost, how long it runs, how many children can come, washrooms and somewhere to eat all need a call to the park before you plan anything.

programs.name: Self-guided park visit
programs.description: The Long Beach Unit is the road-accessible part of the park reserve. It holds beaches, hiking trails and the ʔapsčiik t̓ašii multi-use pathway, which extends 25 km from the southern to the northern boundary of the unit and is used on foot, by stroller, by wheelchair and by bicycle. The park refers to visitors holding a valid National Park Entry Pass, but no entry price, group rate or opening hours could be read. Guided activities and tours in all units are available from licensed commercial operators, not from the park.
programs.what_children_do: Walk or push a stroller along the flat ʔapsčiik t̓ašii pathway, then go down onto the open beaches and into the forest trails of the Long Beach Unit.
programs.our_note: This is all outdoors on an exposed coast, so pack rain gear and a dry change of clothes even in summer. Getting in needs a park pass and the price is not published, so settle what a group pays and where you buy it before you set off.
programs.practical_summary: The multi-use pathway is described as usable with a stroller or a wheelchair, but the beaches and forest trails are not. Washrooms, somewhere indoors to eat, rain shelter, bus parking and the park's own address are not stated, so it is worth a call before you book.
programs.evidence: ʔapsčiik t̓ašii multi-use pathway extends 25 km from the southern to the northern boundary of the Long Beach Unit.
